content: Before I knew to call His name, He came to find me where I lay. He did not wait for me to change; He loved me first and showed the way. So grace arrived before my plea, a gift that set the prisoner free.
I brought no coin to pay the cost, no merit and no claim. I came as one already lost, and left with a new name. What I could never earn or buy, He gave, and did not ask me why.
Grace falls softly like the rain on fields too dry to yield, it washes every dusty stain and greens the barren field. No farmer earns the summer shower, and none of us the saving hour.
When I am weak and running dry, His grace is still enough. When every road seems steep and high, and every path is rough, I lean on One who will not fail, whose mercy stands when we grow frail.
Upon a rough and wooden beam the Son of God was nailed. What looked like loss and broken dream was love that never failed. The darkest day the world has known became the door that leads us home.
The hill was bare, the sky was gray, the crowd had turned to jeer. Yet there my debt was put away, and heaven drew so near. I kneel beside that lonely tree and find the love that died for me.
He bowed His head and gave His breath, the payment fully made. He walked straight through the gate of death, and was not once afraid. It is finished, rang His cry, and sin itself was made to die.
The crown He wore was sharp with thorn, the robe was mockery. He bore the scorn that I had borne, and bore it willingly. Now every thorn that pierces me, He knows, for He has felt the tree.
The nails were driven, cruel and cold, through hands that healed the blind. Yet mercy flowed in streams untold for every lost mankind. The hands we wounded opened wide to hold us safe at Jesus side.
The temple veil was torn in two from top to bottom wide. The way to God was opened new the hour the Savior died. No longer kept outside the door, we enter in forevermore.
There is a blood that speaks of peace, more clear than any word. It brings the guilty sweet release, the cry of heaven heard. No stain so deep it cannot cleanse, no wound so wide it cannot mend.
Behold the Lamb who takes away the sin of all the earth. He did not falter, did not stray, but proved His matchless worth. The spotless One was offered up, and drank for us the bitter cup.
The stone was rolled, the grave was bare, the linen folded neat. The angels said, He is not there, go tell it in the street! The One they buried lives again, the Lord of life, the Friend of men.
The garden held a morning glow that no one had foreseen. The women came in grief and woe and found the grave swept clean. The sun rose slow on Easter day, but the Son had risen first to stay.
Death, where is your bitter sting? Grave, where is your win? The risen Christ is King of kings, He conquered death and sin. We need not fear the final night, for Jesus brings eternal light.
She wept beside the empty stone and thought the gardener near. Then Jesus called her by her own dear name, and all was clear. He calls us too, by name, by grace, and lets us see His living face.
Two walked the road with heavy hearts, a stranger at their side. He opened up the sacred parts of all the prophets cried. And when He broke the bread that night, their eyes were opened to the light.
Thomas would not trust the word until he touched the scars. Then Jesus came, and Thomas heard, and fell beneath the stars. My Lord, my God, the doubter said, believing in the risen Head.
He is risen, rings the call from every grateful tongue. He is risen, Lord of all, the old song and the young. Let every heart and every voice in resurrection hope rejoice.
The seed goes down into the ground and seems to sleep and die. But soon a living shoot is found that reaches for the sky. So Christ went down and rose again, and we shall rise with Him, amen.
The stars above a sleeping town looked down on hay and stall, where God Himself had stepped down to be the Lord of all. A baby cried in Bethlehem, and heaven bent to stay with them.
The shepherds watched their flock by night, the hills were cold and still. Then glory broke in blazing light upon the lonely hill. Fear not, the angel sang that day, a Savior sleeps in manger hay.
No palace held the newborn King, no velvet and no gold. A feeding trough, a humble thing, kept Him from winter cold. The Maker of the stars above lay small and wrapped in mother love.
From distant lands the wise men came, a star to be their guide. They knelt before the holy Name with gifts held close beside. Still wise are those who seek Him now and come to Him with humble bow.
Emmanuel, our God is near, He did not stay away. He came in flesh to draw us here and walk with us each day. In every sorrow, every fear, the name still whispers, God is here.
I light a candle in the dark to mark the holy birth. A tiny flame, a little spark, yet warmth for all the earth. For Christ, the Light, has come to stay, and night must yield to coming day.
Young Mary held her newborn Son and pondered in her heart, the angel words, the promised One, the Savior set apart. She treasured every quiet sign, the human child, the Lord divine.
Joseph took the road of trust and did what God had said. He worked with wood and sawdust and kept the family fed. A quiet man, a faithful friend, who guarded heaven to the end.
The snow comes down on Christmas Eve and blankets field and town. And all of us who dare believe can lay our burdens down. For on this night so long ago, the King came down to us below.
I carried guilt for many years, a weight I could not drop. I brought it to Him with my tears, and there the ache could stop. For Jesus took it on the tree, and now the debt is gone from me.
As far as east is from the west, He casts my sin away. He gives the weary soul its rest and turns my night to day. He does not keep a ledger long; He blots it out and gives a song.
How many times must I forgive the brother who has wronged? As many as the days I live, as many as my song. For I have been forgiven much, and mercy flows from mercy touch.
The prodigal came down the road in rags and hungry shame. The father ran to lift his load and called him by his name. So God runs out to meet us still, and welcomes home the wayward will.
Though scarlet was the stain I wore, He made it white as snow. The crimson spot I mourned before is gone, I know, I know. Washed clean by grace, I stand today, my sin forever rolled away.
A thief hung dying on a cross and turned to Christ in need. He had no time to mend his loss, no good work and no deed. Yet Jesus said, today with Me, in paradise you soon shall be.
His mercy does not wear out thin or run out by the night. Each time I fail and fall again, He sets my footing right. Not once, not twice, but every day, His mercy finds me on the way.
I held a grudge like burning coal and thought it hurt my foe. But it was searing my own soul, and Jesus told me so. I open up my hand at last, and let the Savior heal the past.
Three times he swore he never knew the Man he loved the best. Three times the risen Jesus drew his heart back to its rest. Do you love Me? the Savior said, and gave him lambs and sheep to tend.
My debt was more than I could pay, a mountain built of sin. But Christ stepped in on judgment day and let the pardon in. Paid in full, the record reads, by Him who met my deepest needs.
There is no condemnation now for those in Christ the Son. The judge has lifted up my brow and said the work is done. I walk in freedom, not in fear, for perfect love has brought me near.
On Friday all the earth grew still, the sun withdrew its light. Upon a cruel and rocky hill, the Lord went into night. But do not weep as those who mourn, for Sunday comes, and hope is born.
The Saturday was long and gray, the friends were hid in fear. They did not know that coming day would make the meaning clear. When God seems silent in the tomb, remember Sunday breaks the gloom.
They waved the palms and shouted praise as Jesus rode in town. A humble donkey through the maze, no army and no crown. The King of peace comes gentle still, to ride into the heart and will.
He knelt and washed their dusty feet, the Master as a slave. He broke the bread and poured the sweet red wine, His life He gave. Remember Me, He told them then, and we remember Him again.
Beneath the olive trees He prayed, His sweat like drops of blood. Not My will, Father, He said, and faced the coming flood. Because He bowed in that dark place, I live forever in His grace.
I thought that I was doing fine and needed help from none. Then grace exposed this heart of mine and all that I had done. Now humbled, I can finally see that grace was always meant for me.
I need not borrow strength for years or store up grace for tomorrow. Each day He meets my present fears and carries every sorrow. Like manna in the morning dew, His grace for today is fresh and new.
There is no crown without a cross, the Savior showed us so. He counted glory worth the loss and bore the blow on blow. And now He wears the crown of light, and calls us to the same delight.
He rose above the Bethany hill, the clouds received Him high. The angels said, He is coming still, the same way through the sky. So look up, church, and work and pray, for He returns again one day.
The first man fell beneath the tree and brought the curse to all. The second Adam set us free and broke the ancient fall. In Adam all of us have died, in Christ we live and stand beside.
Redeemed, how sweet to say the word, bought back at heavy price. The slave set free, the captive heard, by Jesus sacrifice. I am not my own, but His alone, and He has made my heart His throne.
What kind of love would leave the sky to walk on dusty sod? What kind of love would choose to die? The holy love of God. No higher price was ever paid, no greater love was ever made.
The old is gone, the new has come, in Christ I am made new. No longer bound and deaf and dumb, my heart is born anew. He takes the broken and the worn, and out of ashes I am born.
The wood that held the baby Lord would one day hold Him high. The manger and the cross accord, He came to us to die. So when we sing of Christmas morn, remember why the King was born.
From His fullness we receive grace upon grace each day. Enough for every soul to believe, enough to light the way. Like ocean waves upon the shore, His grace keeps coming, more and more.

In the night watches I remember You, when the house is dark and the clock ticks slow. Your faithfulness is old and true, Your care is all I need to know. I lie awake but not alone, for You are near and on the throne.

The One who keeps me does not sleep, He does not doze or tire. He watches over all His sheep through darkness, flood, and fire. So close your eyes and rest your head, the Keeper stands beside your bed.
At midnight when the world is still, I bring my heart to You. I lay my worries on the sill and wait the whole night through. You hear the whisper, hear the sigh, and answer from Your throne on high.

It is three in the morning and sleep will not come, my thoughts like a river that runs. But You are the Lord of the dark and the dawn, the Maker of moons and of suns. So I will be still and lean on Your arm, and trust You to keep me from harm.

He counts the stars and calls their names, not one of them is lost. He keeps the glowing heavenly flames and knows their every cost. If He can tend each distant light, He will not lose you in the night.
A lamp burns in the window late for someone on the road. The Father too will watch and wait to help us bear our load. However far the night has gone, His light is on, His light is on.
When sleep has fled and fears arise like shadows on the wall, I turn my heart and lift my eyes to Him who made it all. His peace comes softly as the dew, and stills my soul the whole night through.
The moon rides silver over hills, a witness in the sky. Its gentle glow the valley fills, as quiet hours go by. And every beam that lights the land reflects the work of His own hand.
His mercies meet me with the sun, fresh as the morning dew. Yesterday is past and done, and all today is new. How faithful is my God to me, as constant as the rolling sea.
The east grows pink, the shadows flee, the birds begin to sing. Another day He gives to me, another offering. Lord, take this morning, take it all, and let me answer when You call.
Before I check the news or phone, before the coffee brews, I come to You, my Lord alone, to hear Your better news. Speak first into this waking day, and guide my feet along the way.
Weeping may stay for a night, but joy comes with the dawn. The tears that fell are taken in light, the heavy hour is gone. So hold on, friend, through dark and pain, for morning always comes again.
The rooster crows, the dark is done, the farm begins to stir. I thank the Lord for rising sun and all the gifts that were. And as the light spills on the hay, I ask Him walk with me today.
When grief comes in like heavy tide and pulls me far from shore, I find my Savior at my side, the One who went before. He wept beside a friend once too, and so He knows what I go through.
The shortest verse holds deepest care, Jesus wept, it says. He stood with Mary in despair and shared her darkest days. So weep, dear friend, but not alone, for Christ is weeping with His own.
There is an empty chair tonight where someone used to be. I miss their laughter, miss their light, their hand that held to me. But they are home where none can grieve, and I will see them, I believe.
He keeps our tears within a jar, He counts them one by one. Not one is lost, however far, beneath the moon or sun. And one day He will wipe them dry, with no more need to say goodbye.
The house is quiet, coffee for one, the bed too wide and cold. But God has seen what grief has done, and He will have and hold. He is a husband to the lone, and makes the widowed heart His own.
We grieve, but not as those who have no hope beyond the grave. We bury, but we do not stop believing He can save. The parting is a short goodbye; we meet again beyond the sky.
Fear not, He says, for I am near, I hold you by the hand. When rivers rise I will be here, and you will safely stand. The fire will not consume your soul, for I will keep you, make you whole.
He keeps in perfect peace the mind that stays on Him alone. The worried and the weary find their rest before His throne. So fix your thoughts on Christ above, and rest within His steady love.
My heart was racing, full of dread about the days ahead. Then softly in my soul He said, give Me your fear instead. I opened up my clenched-tight hand, and found a peace I cannot understand.
Be still and know that I am God, the quiet voice still calls. Above the noise, above the clod, above the crumbling walls. So hush, my heart, and cease to strive, for God is near and God alive.
My peace I leave, the Savior said, not as the world gives peace. Let not your heart be troubled, fed by fears that never cease. His peace is deeper than the sea and calmer than the night can be.
I shut the door and kneel to pray where no one else can see. The Father hears what I would say and draws so near to me. In secret places, small and plain, His presence falls like gentle rain.
I asked for things I did not get and wondered if He heard. But looking back I see it yet, His wiser, kinder word. Sometimes the answer we call no is love that will not let us go.
Some nights I have no words to say, my prayer is just a sigh. The Spirit takes it all the way and lifts it up on high. He groans for me when I am weak, and speaks the words I cannot speak.
Our Father, how the words begin, a family and a home. Not distant, cold, or locked within, but near to all who come. We call Him Father, child to friend, and He will keep us to the end.
Lord, I pray for one who strayed and wandered far from You. Remember all the prayers I prayed, and bring them safely through. However long the road may be, bring my beloved home to Thee.

There is a place worn by my knees beside the bed at night. Where I have brought my pleas and please, and found the Lord of light. No grander chapel could I find than this small place where He is kind.

The Shepherd knows each sheep by name and leads them where they need. Through mountain cold and summer flame, He goes ahead to feed. And when one wanders off alone, He searches till He brings it home.
He leads me down to pastures green and waters calm and deep. He shows me paths I have not seen and watches while I sleep. My cup runs over, full and bright, His goodness follows day and night.
He left the ninety nine at rest to find the one astray. He crossed the cliffs and searched the crest and would not walk away. And when He found that trembling lamb, He bore it home on gentle arm.
Though I walk through the valley low, where shadows gather near, I will not fear, for this I know, my Shepherd is right here. His rod and staff will comfort me, until the open field I see.
My sheep will hear My voice, He said, and they will follow Me. Among the many voices spread, His is the one I see. I know the sound of Love that calls, and follow Him past cliffs and walls.
I lift my eyes up to the hills, from where will my help come? My help is from the Lord who fills the sky and earth and sun. He will not let my foot be moved; His care for me is ever proved.
God is my refuge and my strength, a help when trouble calls. Though mountains fall to any length, and every fortress falls, I will not fear, the Lord is near, the God of Jacob holds me here.
Beneath His wings I shelter deep, like chicks beneath the hen. He covers me when storms would sweep, and gathers me again. No arrow, plague, or terror wild can touch the Father and His child.
Taste and see that God is good, the psalmist sang it true. He fills the hungry as He should, and makes the old heart new. Blessed is the one who hides within the shelter where the Lord abides.
Deep calls to deep, the waters roar, Your waves have gone over me. Yet in the night Your song is more than all the raging sea. Why are you downcast, O my soul? Hope still in God, who makes you whole.
He put a new song in my mouth, a hymn of praise to God. He pulled me up from pit and drouth and set me on firm sod. And many will see it and fear, and trust the Lord who brought me here.
Search me, O God, and know my heart, try me and know my ways. See if there is a hidden part that turns from You and strays. And lead me in the ancient road that bears me home with lightened load.

Where could I go to flee from You, or hide from Your bright face? If I fly high or sink down too, You fill each farthest place. The night is not too dark for You; Your hand will hold me, guide me through.
Bless the Lord, O soul of mine, forget not all His ways. He heals, forgives, and is so kind, and crowns me all my days. He satisfies my years with good and renews me as an eagle would.
My soul is restless as the wind and cannot find its rest, till it returns to Him again and settles on His breast. Return, my soul, the Lord is kind; in Him alone true rest you find.
While others sleep, I clock in late and work the quiet hours. Lord, meet me here at midnight gate, and fill me with Your powers. The world may never know my name, but You see all, and love the same.

She walks the hall at half past two with water, pills, and care. Lord, bless the nurse who sees it through, and keep her in Your prayer. Each gentle touch, each patient word, is service seen and love that is heard.

The highway hums beneath the wheels, the white lines rolling past. Lord, keep the driver when he feels the miles are long and vast. Ride with him through the lonely night, and bring him home by morning light.
The watchman on the city wall keeps vigil through the night. He waits for dawn to end it all and bring the morning light. My soul waits for the Lord much more than watchmen wait for dawn to pour.
To you who listen in the dark, alone or wide awake, there is a hope, a holy spark, a love that will not break. The Lord is near in every room; His light can pierce the deepest gloom.

Blessed are they who mourn, He said, for they shall comforted be. The Lord will lift the bowed down head and set the sorrowed free. Your tears are seen, your grief is known, you do not walk this road alone.

When sleep will not come and the hours drag on, I will speak the Name I know. Jesus, keep me until the dawn, and let Your mercy flow. I give You every racing thought, and rest in all that You have bought.
The Lord is near, do not be anxious, pray in everything. With thanks, make known your requests, and lift your offering. Then peace that passes all we know will guard your heart and mind below.
I lie down and I sleep in peace, for You alone, O Lord, make me to dwell in safe release, kept by Your faithful word. The day is done, my work is through, and I commit the night to You.
Another night You kept me well, another dawn I see. More than a tongue could ever tell, Your kindness covers me. I rise to thank You, Lord, again, for keeping me, my dearest Friend.

He set the mountains in their place and carved the valleys low. He spread the sky in boundless space and told the seas to flow. And yet this God of mighty hand still knows each grain of shifting sand.
The ocean roars its endless hymn, the breakers clap their hands. From farthest edge to nearest rim, it praises as it stands. And I, who stand upon the shore, join in and praise my Maker more.
Not one small sparrow falls to ground without the Father knows. And you are worth much more, I found, than every bird that goes. So do not fear what may befall; the God of sparrows holds you all.
Consider how the lilies grow, they neither toil nor spin. Yet Solomon in all his show was never dressed like them. If God so clothes the passing grass, He will not let your needs go past.
The voice of God is in the storm, the thunder shakes the trees. His glory takes a mighty form above the roaring seas. And in His temple all cry out, Glory! with a holy shout.
The sun goes down in gold and rose, the sky a painted page. The Artist who made all of those is Lord of every age. I thank Him for the day now done, and for the setting of the sun.
The heavens tell the glory of God, the skies proclaim His hand. Without a voice they speak abroad to every distant land. Day pours out speech to day again, and night reveals His knowledge then.

The furrows open, dark and deep, the seed is gently sown. The farmer trusts while seedlings sleep that God will make them grown. So too we plant the Word with prayer, and trust the Lord of harvest there.

The summer fields are green and high, the gardens full and sweet. The long days stretch beneath the sky, with bread enough to eat. Lord, in the season of plenty, keep my heart from forgetting, You I seek.
The autumn leaves let go with grace and drift down gold and red. They do not cling to their old place but trust the earth instead. Teach me, Lord, to loosen too, and let my seasons rest in You.
The winter ground is hard and white, the branches bare and thin. But underneath, beyond our sight, new life is stirring in. When seasons of the soul are cold, God keeps the promise He foretold.
The harvest gathered, barns are full, the work of months is done. We give God thanks for every pull of plow and every sun. He gave the seed, He sent the rain, and we rejoice in golden grain.
While earth remains, the Lord has said, seedtime and harvest stay. The cold and heat, the white and red, the night and then the day. The seasons turn by His command, and all of time is in His hand.
Gray hair is a crown of splendor earned along the righteous way. The years have made the spirit tender, closer every day. And even when the strength is spent, His grace remains, His love is lent.
Even to your old age, I am He, and to gray hairs I carry you. I made you, and I hold you free, I bear you all life through. So fear not, aged one, the end; you rest in the arms of your best Friend.
Her hymnal opens on its own to pages she loves most. The binding worn, the paper grown soft as a gentle ghost. She hums the tunes she knew as a girl, and holds to Christ in a changing world.
My grandfather prayed for me by name before I ever knew. His prayers still echo just the same, and God still sees them through. The prayers of saints who go before are stored in heaven evermore.

The righteous flourish like the palm and grow like cedar tall. They still bear fruit in later calm, and stay green through the fall. They tell the world the Lord is just, my Rock, in whom I put my trust.
The children ran to see His face, the grown ups sent them back. But Jesus opened wide His space and said, they do not lack. Let little children come to Me, for such the kingdom is to be.

Sleep now, little one, the Lord is near, He watches through the night. He holds you close and keeps you here until the morning light. And angels guard the little bed where sleeps my child with drowsy head.
Lord, guard the children in my care, so small and so unsure. I cannot keep them everywhere, but You are strong and pure. Where I must let them go and grow, Your arms are under them, I know.
I bless my child in Jesus name, may God be good to you. May He keep you through each flame and see your journey through. And when my years on earth are done, may you still walk with God the Son.
Before you were born, He knew your days, He wrote them in His book. He made you in a hundred ways, He formed your every look. You are no accident or chance, but held within His loving glance.
Two hearts that stood before the Lord and promised all their days, now bound together by His word in hard and gentle ways. A threefold cord is not quickly torn, when Christ is in the vow once sworn.

So many years we walked as one through sickness and through health. We shared the rain, we shared the sun, in poverty and wealth. Lord, thank You for this faithful friend, and keep us both until the end.
Love is patient, love is kind, it does not boast or swell. It keeps no record held in mind of wrongs it knows too well. It bears, believes, and hopes always, and never fails through all our days.

The house we built is not on sand but on the Rock of God. Through storm and flood it still will stand, though tested by the rod. Unless the Lord should build the house, we labor long in vain, my spouse.
Whatever task my hands may find, I do it for the Lord. With willing heart and steady mind, He is my true reward. The dishes, desk, the field, the plow, can all be holy service now.
The Lord once worked with saw and plane in Nazareth of old. He knew the sweat, He knew the strain, the splinter and the cold. So every worker, tired and worn, is known by Him who too was born.
It is Monday and the work begins, the alarm, the drive, the line. Lord, keep my heart from petty sins, and let Your goodness shine. Make me a light in office halls, a quiet hope within the walls.

Six days we labor, sweat, and strive, the seventh He gave for rest. To pause and know that we are alive, and by His hand are blessed. Lay down your tools and lift your eyes; the Lord of rest is good and wise.
They who wait upon the Lord renew their strength each day. They mount on wings, as says the word, and soar above the gray. They run and do not weary fall, they walk and do not faint at all.
I prayed and waited many years, the answer did not come. I watered every seed with tears, my lips grew tired and numb. But God was working all the while, and now I see His patient style.
When hope is put off, the heart grows sick and waits in weary pain. But God is never slow or quick; His timing is not vain. The vision tarries, wait for it, it will surely come, though slow it sit.
Old Abraham looked at the stars and counted them in vain. Yet God had promised from afar, and promise would remain. When Isaac came in later years, God turned to laughter all his tears.
I sit here in the waiting room, the clock hands crawling round. My heart is full of fear and gloom, my thoughts make no sound. But You are here in this cold place, and I can rest within Your grace.
Lord, I believe, help my unbelief, the anxious father cried. And Jesus did not turn in grief, but healed the boy inside. So bring Him all your doubts and fears; He listens kindly, dries your tears.

When God seems far and heaven still, and prayers bounce off the ceiling, I choose to trust His hidden will, apart from what I am feeling. The sun still shines behind the cloud, and He still hears, though not out loud.

If you have faith like mustard seed, the smallest of them all, it moves the mountains of your need and makes the barriers fall. Not great faith, but a great God true, will carry weak believers through.
John sat in prison, sent to ask, are You the One to come? And Jesus did not take to task, but told of blind and dumb. The lame now walk, the poor now hear; go tell him, John, the King is here.

I count the blessings, one by one, the bread, the breath, the bed. The friends, the light of morning sun, the Word by which I am fed. And when the list grows long and wide, I find my heart is satisfied.

In everything give thanks, the Word says plain, not just the good and bright. Give thanks within the loss and pain, give thanks in darkest night. For God is working all for good to those who love Him as they should.
Around the table, hand in hand, we bow our heads and pray. We thank You, Lord, for food and land, and family here today. And for the empty chairs as well, we trust You keep them where they dwell.
For coffee warm and blanket soft, for robin on the sill, for every prayer sent up aloft, for quiet and for still, I lift my thanks to God above, the Giver of all things in love.
If you are lonely in the night, with no one there to call, the Lord has kept you in His sight, He sees you, one and all. He sets the lonely in a home, you never truly walk alone.
I will never leave you, He has said, nor will I forsake. Through every tear that you have shed, through every heart that breaks, He stays beside you, faithful still, through every valley, every hill.
They called Him friend of sinners, scorned for eating with the lost. But He was glad to be adorned with that name, at any cost. And I, a sinner, find in Him the dearest Friend when lights grow dim.
If you are spending Christmas alone, with no one at the door, remember Jesus left His throne to dwell among the poor. He came for hearts that feel unseen, to be the Friend where none have been.
Out in the desert Hagar wept, a mother cast aside. But God who saw her where she slept came near and was her guide. You are the God who sees me, she said, and found a well where she was led.

The phone does not ring much these days, the visits have grown rare. But God remains in all your ways, a constant, faithful care. He counts your hours, He knows your name; His love for you is still the same.
The Potter shapes the spinning clay with patient, skillful hand. He presses, molds, and smooths away until the vessel stands. Lord, shape me as You think is best, and in Your hands I will find rest.
The rainbow arcs across the sky, a sign of promise kept. God hung it there for every eye that ever feared or wept. He keeps His word through flood and fire; His faithfulness will never tire.

No two snowflakes fall the same, each crafted, small, and bright. The God who gives each one its frame will keep you in His sight. If He takes care with frozen dew, how much more care He takes with you.
Halfway along, the years fly fast, the mirror shows the gray. Lord, help me not to chase the past, but walk with You today. The best is not behind, I know; with You, there is more room to grow.
A gentle rain falls on the roof and hushes all the town. It seems to me a quiet proof that grace comes softly down. It does not shout or force its way, but soaks the soil, and life will stay.
Ruth gleaned behind the harvest hands, a stranger far from home. She left behind her native lands to make the Lord her own. And God who saw her loyal heart gave her in David line a part.
Where you go I will go too, Ruth said to Naomi. Your people and your God are true, and there I too will be. And loyal love that would not leave became the line where kings were conceived.
Naomi said, call me bitter now, the Lord has dealt with me. But God was working, though not how her grieving eyes could see. He filled her arms with grandson sweet, and made her empty life complete.
A shepherd boy with stones and sling stepped out before the foe. He trusted in the Lord, his King, and laid the giant low. The battle is the Lord, he cried, and so our giants fall beside.
He tended sheep on Bethlehem hills and played his harp at night. He learned the Lord in quiet stills before he learned to fight. And God, who looks upon the heart, chose him to play the kingly part.
When David fell and Nathan came and said, you are the man, the king fell down in grief and shame, and cried, have mercy, then. Create in me a heart made clean, and God restored what might have been.
Elijah ran and sat to die beneath a broom tree wide. But God sent bread down from the sky and water at his side. Sleep now and eat, the angel said, the journey long, but you are fed.
The wind went by, the mountain shook, the fire passed and blazed. But God was not in all that took Elijah so amazed. Then came a whisper, soft and low, and there the Lord was, still and slow.
Upon Mount Carmel, prophets cried to Baal from dawn to night. Then one man prayed, and fire supplied came down in blazing light. The Lord, He is the God, they said, and fell before Him, bowing head.
Behold the handmaid of the Lord, young Mary softly said. Be it to me as in Your word, though fear was in her head. And by her yes, the Son was born; her trust opened the brightest morn.
My soul proclaims the Lord is great, said Mary in her song. He lifts the lowly from their state, and humbles all the strong. He fills the hungry, keeps His word, and mercy flows from Him, the Lord.
Peter stepped out on the sea, his eyes on Jesus face. He walked on waves so wondrously, then fear took up its place. He sank and cried, Lord, rescue me! And Jesus caught him, faithfully.
Leave your nets and follow Me, said Jesus by the shore. And Peter left the boat and sea to fish for something more. So still He calls from daily task, to follow Him is all He asks.

Saul rode out breathing threats and rage to bind the church in chains. A light from heaven turned the page and blinded him on plains. The persecutor turned to praise, and Paul preached Christ through all his days.
At midnight in the prison cell, with backs all bruised and torn, Paul and Silas sang so well that chains fell off by morn. So sing, though dark the night may be; your praise can set the captive free.
I know what plenty is, said Paul, and I know hunger too. Through Christ who strengthens, I can all, whatever I go through. Contentment is not found in gold, but in the hand of Christ we hold.
A bush that burned but did not burn caught Moses on the hill. Take off your shoes, he came to learn, for this is holy still. I AM has sent you, God declared, and Moses went, though he was scared.

The sea before, the chariots near, the people cried in fright. But Moses said, stand still, no fear, and watch the Lord in might. The waters parted, walls of blue, and God made paths where none came through.
Sold by brothers, jailed in shame, forgotten in the dark. Yet Joseph kept the Lord the same, and God still left His mark. What you meant for harm, he said, God meant for good, and bread was spread.
Daniel prayed with windows wide, as he had done before. They threw him into lions inside and sealed the stony door. But God sent angels in the night, and shut the jaws before they bite.
They would not bow to golden gods, though fire was heated hot. They faced the king against all odds, and trusted in their lot. And in the flames a fourth was seen, the Son of God, who walked between.
Perhaps you came for such a time, her uncle said to her. So Esther took the risk sublime, though death was likely there. If I perish, then I perish, she said, and God saved the people she led.

Noah built when skies were clear, and neighbors laughed and stared. He trusted God through all the jeer, and hammered, warned, and cared. And when the rain began to pour, God shut him safely in the door.

Hannah prayed with lips that moved and not a sound came out. The priest thought she was drunk, unmoved, but God heard all her doubt. He gave her Samuel, her son, and she gave him back when it was done.
Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears, young Samuel replied. Three times God called in temple years, and there the boy complied. Teach us to listen in the night, as Samuel did, by lamp and light.
Jonah ran the other way and sailed toward the west. But God sent storm and fish that day to put his flight to rest. And from the belly of the deep, he prayed, and God renewed his keep.
A little man climbed up a tree to see the Lord go by. And Jesus stopped and said, with Me you dine today, come nigh. The tax man changed, gave back fourfold; salvation came to young and old.
She came at noon to draw alone, to dodge the town and talk. But Jesus met her by the stone and offered living stock. He knew her past and loved her still, and she ran home with joy to spill.
Four days within the tomb he lay, the sisters wept their grief. Then Jesus came and prayed that day, and spoke with sure belief. Lazarus, come forth! He cried, and out he came, still bound, alive.
By Jericho a blind man cried, Son of David, mercy please! The crowd rebuked, but he replied louder than the breeze. And Jesus stopped and called him near, and opened eyes to see Him clear.

She dropped two coins into the box, the smallest gift of all. The rich gave much from heavy stocks, but hers was not so small. She gave her all, the Savior said, and blessed the hand that gave her bread.
Martha worked with pots and plates, distracted, stressed, and tired. Mary sat by Jesus gates and listened, so inspired. One thing is needed, Jesus said, sit at My feet and be fed.
He came by night to ask in secret what this teacher meant. You must be born again, the Spirit, is how the answer went. For God so loved the world He gave His only Son to seek and save.
Job sat in ashes, lost and sore, his children and wealth gone. Yet still he said, I know once more, my Redeemer lives on. And in my flesh I shall see God, though I am laid beneath the sod.
Jacob wrestled through the night with One he could not see. He held on till the morning light and would not let Him free. He left with limp and blessing new, and Israel was his name, it is true.
With only three hundred men and torch and trumpet bright, Gideon went forth again to face the Midian might. Not by the many, but the Lord, the battle won without a sword.
Old Abraham climbed with his son, the wood upon his back. Where is the lamb? asked the young one. God will provide, no lack. And on the mount the ram was caught, a picture of the Christ He brought.
As stones were flying, Stephen gazed and saw the open sky. The Son of Man stood up, amazed, to welcome him on high. Lord, do not hold this sin, he prayed, forgiving those by whom he was slain.
From childhood Timothy was taught the Scriptures by his kin. His grandmother and mother brought the faith to dwell within. So pass it on to those you love, the faith that comes from God above.
They called him son of comfort, Barnabas the kind. He stood for Paul when others shunned and left the past behind. Be like him, friend, and lift the low, and help the faltering to grow.
By the river Lydia heard the gospel Paul proclaimed. The Lord then opened up her heart, and she was never the same. She opened home and heart and door, and served the Lord forevermore.
John leaned on Jesus at the meal and stood beside the cross. He saw the Savior wounds were real and knew the depth of loss. And old, he wrote, my children dear, love one another, God is near.
Isaiah saw the Lord on high, the train filled temple wide. The seraphs sang, holy, they cry, and he fell down and cried. A coal touched lips, his sin was gone; Here am I, send me, he said on.
They dropped him down into the mud, the prophet of the Lord. But God sent help, His faithful word, a rope, a kindly cord. Though cast down low in mire and shame, God lifted him, and kept his name.
Rahab hung a scarlet cord down from her window high. She trusted in Israel Lord when Jericho would die. And grace took in the outcast one, and wove her into David son.
Old Simeon had waited long to see the promised One. He held the child and sang his song, my waiting days are done. Now let your servant go in peace, my eyes have seen the world release.
Anna prayed both night and day, a widow, old and wise. And when the Child came by that way, she knew Him with her eyes. She told of Him to all who waited, the hope of Israel long awaited.
The servant feared the army near that circled all the town. Elisha prayed, Lord, make it clear, and let his eyes look round. And there were chariots of fire; the hosts of God are always higher.

With trowel in one hand, sword in the other, they built the broken wall. Nehemiah urged each brother to work and heed the call. The joy of the Lord is our strength, he said, and stone by stone the city spread.
The priest walked by, the Levite too, and left the wounded man. A stranger stopped and saw him through, and helped him as he can. Go and do likewise, Jesus said; love is a deed, and not just a creed.
At eighty five old Caleb asked, give me that mountain land. He did not fear the giants massed, the Lord was in his hand. With wholehearted faith he climbed, and claimed the promise just in time.
As for me and my house, said Joshua to the crowd, we will serve the Lord, and so his choice rang strong and loud. Choose this day whom you will serve, and give the Lord your whole reserve.

Just say the word, the soldier said, my servant will be healed. I need not have You by his bed; Your word, Lord, is the shield. And Jesus marveled at such trust, and healed the servant, good and just.

She broke the jar of costly nard and poured it on His feet. She wiped them with her hair unbarred, the fragrance rich and sweet. They called it waste, He called it good, love given freely as it should.
A runaway slave met Paul in jail and found the Lord of grace. Then Paul sent back the letter mail to plead his brother case. Receive him now not as a slave, but as a brother Christ did save.
A little church with steeple white sits by the county road. Its doors swing open Sunday bright to all who bear a load. The pews are worn, the floor is plain, but Christ is honored there again.
We are one body, many parts, the hand, the foot, the eye. We share one Spirit in our hearts, one Lord who reigns on high. No part can say, I need you not, for every member has its lot.
The tables groan with casseroles, the coffee pot is on. We share our bread and share our souls till afternoon is gone. And there among the laughing crowd, the Lord is honored, praised aloud.
We are the living stones He lays to build a holy place. Not brick and mortar, but the praise of people saved by grace. And Christ the cornerstone stands true, holding the old and holding the new.
The church, His bride, is being made both spotless and complete. He washes her, her debt is paid, she waits for Him to meet. And on that day of wedding feast, the greatest guest will be the least.
Where two or three are gathered near, in Jesus holy name, the Lord Himself is with us here, His promise still the same. So small the group, so great the Guest, and in His presence we are blessed.
The pastor sits at midnight still, his sermon not yet done. He seeks the Lord to know His will, to preach the Holy One. Lord, bless the shepherds of Your flock, and keep them steady on the Rock.
Go into all the world, He said, and preach the gospel true. To every tribe the Word be spread, to every nation too. And lo, I am with you always near, until the end of age is here.
She packed her bags and crossed the sea to tell of Jesus name. In village huts beneath the tree, she shared the gospel flame. Far from home, but never alone, she made the love of Jesus known.
How beautiful upon the hills the feet of those who bring good news of peace that heals and fills, and tells of Christ the King. Go, tell the story far and near, and let the waiting nations hear.
The harvest fields are white and wide, the workers all too few. So pray the Lord to send beside more laborers, strong and true. And maybe, friend, the one He sends, is you to reach the world ends.
From every tribe and tongue they come, from every land and sea. They gather round the Lamb as one to worship endlessly. The songs are many, voice is one, all glory to the risen Son.
Remember those who are in chains as if in chains with them. Pray for the church in hidden lanes who suffer for His name. The Lord is with them in the cell, and one day all of them will be well.
Like rushing wind and tongues of flame, the Spirit filled the room. The frightened followers became bold preachers past the gloom. The same Spirit dwells in us today, to lead and guide us on the way.
Spirit of God, blow over me, and fill me fresh again. Revive the dry and dusty tree, and wash me like the rain. Without You I am dust and clay, but with You, life is here to stay.
I will not leave you orphans, He said, I send the Comforter. He lives within, by Him we are led, our guide and our helper. The Spirit of truth within our breast reminds us we are His and blessed.
Love, joy, and peace, and patience too, kindness and goodness grow. Faithfulness and gentle hue, and self control will show. Not by our strength these fruits appear, but by the Spirit living here.
When Jesus rose from Jordan wave, the heavens opened wide. The Spirit like a dove came down and rested at His side. This is My Son, the Father said, in whom My joy is fully spread.
The wind blows where it wishes to, you hear it but not see. So is the Spirit, moving through, and making hearts be free. You cannot trap it, cannot tame, but feel it when He calls your name.
Around the throne the angels cry, holy is the Lord. The seraphs cover face and eye before the living Word. And we, the dust, are called to bring our praises too to God our King.
The Father seeks the ones who come in spirit and in truth. Not just a building, not a drum, not age, and not just youth. But hearts laid open, honest, real, before the throne of God to kneel.
Lift up your hands in holy place and bless the Lord tonight. You servants who behold His face and stand within His light. The Lord who made the heaven and earth will bless you, Zion, with His worth.

The old pump organ wheezed and sighed, the farm wives sang along. The hymns rolled out both deep and wide, a simple, sturdy song. The tune was rough, the words were true, and heaven listened as they flew.
We sing the hymns our parents sang, the words both firm and true. The chapel rafters gently rang with faith both old and new. And every verse, each sacred line, points to the Savior, yours and mine.
We sang beside her hospital bed the hymns she loved so well. Her lips still moved to what we said, her eyes began to swell. And though her voice was nearly gone, the song of heaven carried on.
He gives a song in the night, the Scripture says it plain. When all is dark and out of sight, a melody remains. So hum the hymn you learned as a child, and let your heart be reconciled.
Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all you lands, and sing. Come before Him in accord with gladness to the King. Not perfect pitch but grateful heart is all He asks for us to start.
Up in the choir loft we stand in robes of faded blue. With hymnal open in each hand, we sing the old and new. And though our voices crack with age, we sing for God, our sacred stage.

He is coming back, the angels said, the same way that He went. To raise the living and the dead, with trumpet heaven sent. So keep your lamps trimmed bright and clear, the Bridegroom soon will be appearing here.
One day the trumpet will resound, the dead in Christ will rise. And we who are on earth around will meet Him in the skies. So comfort one another, friend, with words of hope that never end.
No one knows the day or hour, not angels in the sky. So watch and pray with all your power, the Lord is drawing nigh. Be found at work and found in love, when Jesus comes from heaven above.
Maranatha, come, Lord, come, the early church would pray. We long to see Your kingdom come and hasten on the day. Until then, keep us faithful, true, and keep our longing fixed on You.
Every knee will bow one day and every tongue confess, that Jesus Christ is Lord always, the King of righteousness. So bow today in willing praise, before the end of earthly days.
Ten waited for the bridegroom, five had oil and five had none. The careless missed the wedding room, the wise went in as one. So fill your lamp with oil today; the Bridegroom will not long delay.
He comes just like a thief at night, when no one is aware. So live as children of the light, and keep your heart in prayer. Not fearful, but with hope and cheer, for our redemption draws near.
There is a home not made by hand, eternal in the sky. A city in a better land where no one says goodbye. And Jesus went to make it ready, so walk on, pilgrim, slow and steady.
There will be no more death or tears, no mourning and no pain. The former things of all the years will never come again. Behold, He makes all things anew, and wipes the tears from me and you.
In My Father house are many rooms, the Savior told His friends. I go to make a place, He assumes, where love will never end. And I will come and take you there, to be with Me, beyond all care.

The streets are gold, the gates are pearl, the river crystal clear. But more than all the wondrous world, the Lamb Himself is here. Not gold nor gates will be our song, but Jesus, whom we loved so long.
Beside the river, bright and wide, the tree of life will grow. Its leaves will heal on every side the nations here below. And all the curse will pass away, in that unending, glorious day.
Now we see as through a glass, in shadows dim and gray. But one day all of that will pass, and face to face we stay. We will know Him as we are known, and kneel before the shining throne.
There will be no night in heaven, no need for lamp or sun. The Lord Himself the light is given, the glory of the Son. And we who know the long dark hours will rest in everlasting bowers.

A cloud of witnesses surrounds the race that we must run. The saints who passed through earthly bounds now cheer for everyone. So lay aside the weight and sin, and run, for soon we will see them again.
Absent from the body here is present with the Lord. So do not grieve with bitter fear the faithful gone toward. They walk in glory, free from pain, and what was loss for us, is gain.
The holy city coming down, adorned just like a bride. God dwells with men in every town, and wipes the tears they cried. His people, and their God is He, forever, through eternity.
And when I reach that shore at last, I long to hear Him say, well done, the race is run and past, come in and rest today. My faithful servant, enter in, to joy that never ends again.
For God so loved the world He gave His one and only Son, that all who trust Him He would save, the victory is won. Not perish, but have life for good; such is the love of God, understood.
The fire fell on Pentecost, a tongue on every head. The lost were found, the found were tossed into the streets instead. Three thousand came to Christ that day, and the church began to grow and pray.
Down in the water, buried deep, with Christ in death I lay. And up I rise, my soul to keep, to walk a newer way. The old has drowned, the new is here, my Savior lives, and I am clear.
We take the bread, we take the cup, remembering His death. Until He comes, we lift it up, and praise with every breath. His body broken, blood outpoured, we feast together with our Lord.
The Sunday bells ring out across the valley, field, and town. They call the found, they call the lost, to come and settle down. Come worship, come, the bells all say, the Lord has risen, come today.

Lord, make us one as You are one, the Father and the Son. Let quarrels cease, let love be spun, till all our hearts are won. That the world may know that You were sent, by how the church in love is spent.
We gather in a living room with Bibles on our knees. We share our joys and share our gloom, our struggles and our pleas. And Jesus sits among the chairs, and listens to our humble prayers.
She taught us songs with felt and glue, the stories bright and plain. Of Noah, Daniel, and Jesus too, of sunshine and of rain. She planted seeds in children small that grew to answer heaven call.
I worship You with tears tonight, I do not understand. But even in the dimming light I hold Your steady hand. My praise is broken, but still true, and I will give it all to You.
The boat was tossed, the waves were high, the frightened sailors cried. Then Jesus woke beneath the sky and spoke above the tide. Peace, be still, He said, and lo, the wind lay down, the sea lay low.

The sky turns green, the sirens wail, the storm comes rolling through. We huddle low beneath the hail and call, Lord, see us through. And when it passes, still we stand, held safe within the Father hand.
We have this hope, an anchor sure, that holds within the veil. Though winds may howl and tides obscure, this anchor will not fail. Fastened to the Rock above, it holds us by eternal love.
When you pass through the waters deep, I will be there with you. The rivers will not overleap, I will carry you through. For I am the Lord, your God alone, you are precious, and you are My own.

The storm has passed, the clouds are torn, the sunlight breaks anew. The broken branches, fields once worn, are washed with diamond dew. And God, who walked us through the night, now paints the sky with morning light.
Lord, as the winds begin to rise along the coastal shore, protect the homes, the old, the wise, the poor, and rich, and more. And when the waters come and go, help neighbors love, and kindness grow.
He touched the leper, cleansed the skin, He made the lame to stand. He opened ears to let sound in, and healed with gentle hand. The Healer walks among us still, to mend the body, soul, and will.
By His stripes we have been healed, Isaiah wrote of old. The wounds He bore have been revealed as grace both rich and bold. Whatever sickness we may know, His healing love will overflow.
In the little hospital chapel, lit by a single light, a father kneels in prayer to grapple with the coming night. Lord, hold my child within Your care, and let him know that You are there.

The pain is here when I awake and stays through all the day. Lord, give me grace for every ache, and strength to walk the way. Your power is perfect in my weakness, and You will crown it all with sweetness.

She pressed through crowds to touch His hem, twelve years she bled in shame. Her faith reached out, and there and then, the healing power came. Daughter, He said, your faith is sound, go now in peace, for you are found.
Some wounds are hidden deep inside where no one else can see. He binds the broken, the denied, and sets the captive free. The Healer of the heart is near, to mend the hurt of many a year.
Lord, in the chemo chair today, the needle in my arm, I ask You, stay with me, I pray, and keep my heart from harm. Whatever news the doctor brings, I rest beneath Your mighty wings.
Lord, bless the soldier far from home, in desert or in snow. Wherever duty bids him roam, wherever he must go. Be his shield and his strong tower, and bring him home in Your good hour.

Put on the armor of the Lord, the belt of truth and peace. Take up the Spirit mighty sword, the faith that will not cease. Stand firm against the darkened powers, for victory, through Christ, is ours.
We thank You, Lord, for those who served and gave their youth away. For every soldier who preserved the freedom of today. Heal the wounds that still remain, and comfort those who bear the pain.

She tucks the children into bed and checks the phone again. Lord, keep her husband safe, she said, and bring him home amen. Give strength to those who wait at home, and let them know they are not alone.

No greater love has any man than this, to lay down life. The Savior showed the perfect plan through sorrow, pain, and strife. And those who give themselves for friends reflect the love that never ends.
The farmer rises before the sun to milk and feed and plow. His work is never really done, the sweat upon his brow. Lord, bless the hands that till the land, and feed the world at Your command.
The fields are cracked, the creek is dry, the corn is bending low. Lord, open up the heavy sky and let the rainfall flow. And if the rain is slow to come, still keep our hearts in faith, not numb.

Those who sow in tears will reap with songs of joy one day. Though weeping, carrying seed to keep, they walk the furrowed way. They will return with shouts of cheer, with sheaves of harvest, gathered here.
The barn is quiet, cattle fed, the swallows tucked away. The farmer bows his weary head and thanks God for the day. For calf and crop, for rain and sun, he prays, Lord, let Thy will be done.

Some seed fell on the beaten track, some fell on rocks and thorn. But some fell on good soil and back came grain in fields of corn. Lord, make my heart the good soil, Lord, to hear and keep Your living word.

Lord, grant us traveling mercies now, on highway, rail, and air. Keep every wheel, and wing, and prow within Your watchful care. Wherever we go, You are already there, and bring us home in answer to prayer.
I am a pilgrim passing through, this world is not my home. My treasure waits beyond the blue, wherever I may roam. So travel light and hold things loose; the road leads home to Christ, no excuse.
The airport hums at midnight late, the gates are mostly bare. A traveler sits there by the gate and bows his head in prayer. Lord, guide me on this journey far, and be my compass, be my star.
The long drive home through rain and dark, the wipers keeping time. I pray for every passing mark, each mile and every climb. And as the headlights sweep the road, I thank You, Lord, for every load.
By faith old Abraham went out, not knowing where to go. He followed God through fear and doubt, and trusted Him to know. So when your path is not yet clear, go forth in faith, for God is near.
The Lord is my rock and fortress strong, my refuge and my shield. When enemies would do me wrong, I will not ever yield. I call upon the Lord, my praise, and He will save me all my days.
He gives strength to the weary one and power to the weak. Even the young, when day is done, grow tired and cannot speak. But those who hope in Him will rise, like eagles soaring in the skies.
The kingdom is a mustard seed, so tiny, small, and plain. It grows into a tree indeed, where birds of heaven remain. Do not despise the small and slow; in God, the smallest things will grow.
Your word, a lamp to light my feet, a light upon my path. It makes the bitter waters sweet, and turns away the wrath. I hide it in my heart each day, so I will not go astray.
Whoever drinks the water here will thirst again, He said. But I give water, living, clear, a spring that keeps you fed. Come, drink from Christ, the fountain free, and thirst no more eternally.
I am the Bread of Life, He said, come eat and hunger not. The manna in the desert spread was given and forgot. But Christ remains, the living Bread, and all who come to Him are fed.
I am the Light of all the world, He said to those who heard. Whoever follows, though the night has swirled, will walk within His word. They will not stumble in the dark, but carry life, a holy spark.
I am the Vine, and you the branch, abide in Me and grow. Apart from Me, you have no chance, but in Me, fruit will show. So stay connected, close and near, and bear the fruit of love and cheer.
I am the way, the truth, the life, the Savior plainly said. Through Him alone, past fear and strife, we come to God instead. No other road, no other name, can bring us home and lift our shame.
reference: The Way the Truth the Life

content: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, worn and tired. I will give rest when life is dreary, and hope when you are mired. My yoke is easy, light, and kind, and rest for souls you will find.
Seek first the kingdom of the Lord and all His righteousness. And all these things, as in His word, He gives to you and blesses. So do not worry, do not fret, the Father has not failed you yet.
Do not worry about tomorrow, it will worry for itself. Each day has trouble, each its sorrow, put fear upon the shelf. The God who holds this day today will hold tomorrow, come what may.
You are the salt that gives the taste, the light that lights the hill. Do not let your life go to waste, but shine for Jesus still. Let others see the good you do, and praise the Father who made you.

The gate is narrow, path is thin that leads to life above. The road is wide that leads to sin, but straight the road of love. Choose well the gate, and walk it true, and Christ will walk it there with you.
Store not your treasure here below where moth and rust destroy. But store it where the angels go, in everlasting joy. For where your treasure is, the heart will follow and never part.
A woman lost a silver coin and swept the house all through. She lit a lamp and searched to join it with the other few. And when she found it, how she sang! So heaven rejoices, all bells rang.
Who is faithful in the small is faithful in the much. So do not scorn a little call, a humble, gentle touch. The cup of water, kindly given, is noticed by the Lord of heaven.
Humble yourself beneath His hand, and He will lift you high. Cast every care at His command, for He is standing by. He cares for you, the Scripture says, in all your nights and all your days.

An old man on the city bus was struggling with his bag. A young girl helped without a fuss, her kindness did not lag. And heaven noticed, though no one cheered, for Christ was in the love that appeared.
Lord, heal our land, we humbly pray, and turn our hearts to You. Forgive the ways we went astray, and make us faithful, true. Bless leaders, neighbors, great and small, and let Your mercy cover all.
Lord, for the one behind the bars who stares at concrete gray, remind him of the shining stars, and of a brighter day. No cell can keep Your love away, no lock can bar You when we pray.

Lord, for the one who fights the chain of bottle, pill, or vice, break through the cycle and the pain, and pay the bitter price. You set the captive free indeed; be all the strength that they will need.
Tonight beneath the overpass a man lies in the cold. Lord, cover him beneath Your grace, and warm him as foretold. And stir our hearts to share our bread, and give the homeless one a bed.
The day is ending, Lord, at last, the lamps are turning low. I thank You for the hours now past, and all the grace You show. Watch over all who rest tonight, and keep them till the morning light.

To all who listen through the night, to hymns and favorite songs, may Jesus keep you in His light, the place where you belong. May peace be yours till break of day, and may His love light up your way.

The Lord bless you and keep you near, His face shine on you bright. May He be gracious, calm your fear, and give you peace tonight. The Lord look on you with His love, and send you blessing from above.
Rest now, dear friend, and know the Lord will hold you safe and sure. His love will keep you by His word, His promise ever pure. So close at last your weary eyes, the Lord is watching from the skies.
